skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Toolkit for testing local web applications with Python Playwright scripts. It helps start local servers, inspect rendered pages, capture screenshots, and collect console logs.
skill.summary: Test and debug local web applications with Playwright automation.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: Most static Markdown and localhost findings are false positives from documentation examples or local debugging artifacts. The helper script does execute user-supplied commands, including shell=True server commands, and the skill text discourages source review before execution.

remediation.issue: Server commands are launched with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Accept server commands as argument arrays, add allowlisted presets, or require explicit confirmation before shell execution.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents not to read bundled script source before use.
remediation.suggestion: Replace black-box guidance with advice to inspect helper behavior and run --help before executing trusted commands.

remediation.issue: Examples use fixed output paths for screenshots and console logs.
remediation.suggestion: Make output paths configurable and document that generated artifacts may contain local application data.

content.value_statement: Local web apps can be hard to verify after JavaScript renders the page. This skill guides Playwright scripts that inspect UI state, capture screenshots, collect logs, and run against local servers.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of Python Playwright scripts for local and dynamic web apps.
Starts one or more local servers before running an automation command.
Captures browser screenshots for visual inspection.
Captures console messages and saves them to a local output file.
Discovers rendered buttons, links, and input fields.
Supports static HTML automation through file URLs.
limitations: It focuses on Python synchronous Playwright examples, not full test framework setup.
Server commands run locally and must be reviewed before execution.
Example URLs and output paths usually need project-specific changes.
It does not provide cross-browser test matrices or cloud browser services.

use_cases.title: Verify Local UI Behavior
use_cases.description: Run Playwright checks against a local development server and confirm important screens behave as expected.

use_cases.title: Debug Rendered Page State
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots, console messages, and rendered DOM details after client-side JavaScript finishes loading.

use_cases.title: Inspect Static Prototypes
use_cases.description: Open local HTML files, interact with visible controls, and capture before-and-after screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Page Screenshot
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a single local page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to open my local web app, wait for the page to finish loading, and capture a full-page screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Find Interactive Elements
prompt_templates.scenario: Discover selectors before writing an automation flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect the rendered page and list visible buttons, links, inputs, and useful selectors.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Browser Console Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnose runtime errors during local testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to run the page, collect browser console messages, and summarize errors or warnings that affect the UI.

prompt_templates.title: Test With Multiple Servers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for apps with separate backend and frontend servers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to start the required local servers after confirming the commands, run the Playwright automation, and clean up the servers.

output_examples.input: Test my local dashboard and report whether the main navigation works.
output_examples.output: The report names each navigation item tested, notes visible page changes, and includes the screenshot location for review.

output_examples.input: Capture browser console output while opening the settings page.
output_examples.output: The result summarizes console errors and warnings, explains likely UI impact, and gives the saved log location.

output_examples.input: Inspect a static HTML form and confirm the submit flow changes the page.
output_examples.output: The result lists discovered form fields, describes the interaction performed, and references before-and-after screenshots.

best_practices: Review helper scripts and confirm server commands before running local command automation.
Wait for network idle or visible selectors before inspecting dynamic pages.
Store screenshots and logs in user-approved workspace output paths.
anti_patterns: Running unknown server commands through the helper without reviewing the arguments.
Inspecting a dynamic page before the application has finished rendering.
Assuming selectors from static HTML always match the rendered application state.

faq.question: Does this skill require Playwright?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Python Playwright with a Chromium browser.

faq.question: Can it test an app that is already running?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can guide scripts that connect to an existing local URL.

faq.question: Can it start local servers?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled helper can start one or more local servers before running automation.

faq.question: Are screenshots supported?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show full-page screenshot capture for rendered pages and static HTML files.

faq.question: Does it send test data to external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The reviewed examples target localhost or local files.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review any server command and output path, especially when using the helper script.
